adjudication_label: batch_8:Indentation model geometry and periodicity constraints
canonical_question: What are the physical justifications and criteria defining the geometric parameters (indentation depth, model lateral dimensions, rubbing direction, and coating thickness) in the high entropy alloy/copper nanoindentation and rubbing simulation?

question_variants.question: Why was the indentation depth limited to 10 Å, and does this depth probe only the surface or the interface between coating and matrix?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The indentation depth of 10 Å is specified in the text as the depth for rubbing along the Y-axis. The text explicitly states the model layers include a 'constant temperature' layer from 5 to 10 Å and a Cu layer starting at 10 Å, implying the 10 Å depth probes the interface/constant temperature region between the coating and the bulk matrix.

answers.answer: The model layer definition specifies a 'constant temperature' layer ranging from 5 to 10 Å and a Cu matrix layer starting at 10 Å (10~55 Å). The text mentions rubbing along the Y axis with a depth of 10 Å. This configuration indicates the 10 Å depth corresponds to the boundary between the constant temperature layer (5-10 Å) and the Cu matrix layer (10-55 Å), effectively probing the interface region or the boundary layer itself.
answers.material: Cu matrix / FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating
answers.processing_state: as-built atomic model with defined layers
answers.measurement_outcome: layer boundaries at 0-5 Å (boundary), 5-10 Å (constant temperature), 10-55 Å (Cu)
answers.mechanism: Layer definition based on depth ranges for thermostat application
answers.boundary_limitation: Depth of 10 Å defines the transition from the constant temperature layer to the Cu matrix
evidence_spans: In the nanoindentation model, single crystal Cu was used as the matrix material and FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy was used as the coating material.
The same lattice types of both materials were set.
The model size of the Cu matrix was 100 Å × 100 Å × 55 Å, and the total number of atoms was 47,111.

source_evidence_spans: with a depth of 10 Å, and then rubbed along the positive direction of the Y axis

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: The simulation parameters (10 Å depth, 100 Å × 100 Å lateral size, Y-axis rubbing, and 21 Å coating thickness) are observed values from the model definition, but the provided text lacks explicit scientific justification, selection criteria, or validation data for any of these specific geometric choices.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: One answer interprets the 10 Å depth as a functional boundary definition between a thermostat layer and the Cu matrix, providing a mechanical rationale for that specific parameter. In contrast, the other answers (regarding lateral size, rubbing direction, and coating thickness) report a total absence of explanatory text in the source material.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The definition of the 10 Å depth is dependent on the specific layering scheme (thermostat 5-10 Å, matrix 10-55 Å), whereas the other parameters appear as fixed inputs without stated dependencies on material properties or simulation conditions in the text.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: No direct contradictions exist between the answers; however, there is an epistemic discrepancy where the 10 Å depth is partially explained as a boundary definition [68191bc52376fb3a], while other similar geometric choices are explicitly flagged as having no provided rationale [9f28c9551958ecb0, ba80aad1e45a21d9, 79b83a0288fc9570].
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: Weak to Non-existent for justification. Evidence is limited to 'observed' values of parameters with 'unspecified' or 'not provided' rationales for their sufficiency or selection.
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: The study fails to report why the 100 Å × 100 Å size prevents periodic image interactions, why the Y-axis was chosen over the X-axis, why the coating is exactly 21 Å, or whether this thickness is sufficient to represent bulk behavior without substrate interference.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The geometric parameters (specifically the 10 Å depth and 21 Å thickness) were selected based on convergence criteria or computational constraints not described in the text, rather than on physical scaling laws or periodicity limits.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Convergence testing of the model by systematically increasing the lateral dimensions beyond 100 Å and the coating thickness beyond 21 Å to determine if friction or deformation properties stabilize, thereby empirically validating the sufficiency of the current dimensions.
